To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the activity of hepatic glucokinas in the rat is affected by the nutritional state of the animal, and that this activity is also affected by X- irradiation.

1) X-irradiaton depressed hepatic glucokinases activity, 2) X-irratiation slowed the rate of decline of hepatic glucokiase activity in fasted rats, 3) the effect of X- irradiation on hepatic glucoikinase was dependent on pituitary gland, 4) hepatic fructoikinase activity was not affected by X- irradiation.
the effects of X-irradation on hepatic enzyme activities are different in fasted and high-glucose-fed animals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of X- irradiation on the activity of hepatic glucokinas and fructokinase and the effect of X - irradiation on the hepatic glycogen content of the normal and hypophysectomised rat.
the effect of X- and γ -irradiation on the activities of some enzymes of carbohydrate metabolism.
the effects of X-iradiation on the regulation of glucokinase in rat liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
X-irradiated animals are more sensitive to dietary manipulation of the activity of the hepatic glucokinases than non-irradiated ones.
the effects of X-iradiation on glucokinases in various tissues of the rat are tissue- and nutritional-specific.
the X-irradiated rat has a decreased capacity for glucose metabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

X-irradiaton has a specific effect on glucokinase activity, but not on other hexokinase activities, and that the effect is related to nutritional conditions and to the activity of the pituitary gland.
X-irradiated rats have an abnormality of hepatic glucokinas, which may be due to an abnormality of the pituitary gland.
X-irradiations' effects on glucokinase activity depend upon the nutritional status of the animal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glucokinase is a key enzyme in the regulation of blood glucose.
X-irradiated animals, especially those subjected to a high-glucose intake, are more susceptible to hypophysectomy and to the development of diabetes than are normal animals.
the effects of X-irradation on hepatic gluco kinase in the rat are dependent on the nutritional state of the animal.
